_about: Mutation adequacy for privileged-mcp-action/v0. ONE genuine hole: the origin leg of the v0 marker triple is promised and unexercised. Two further rules were declared and are NOT holes -- they mutate the wrong stage and the wrong profile -- and are marked out_of_scope with that reasoning rather than dropped, so the mistake stays visible. Independently classified by Ruley against docs/profiles/privileged-mcp-action/v0.md §5 and the Stage 2/3 architecture.

denial_marker_binding.label: 0 an unrecognised marker triple fails closed
denial_marker_binding.reason: WRONG STAGE, not a hole. v0 does promise that an unrecognised in-namespace schema fails closed, but that promise is the Stage 2 arm (other => unknown_profile_schema) at verify_privileged_mcp_action.rs:331, which runs BEFORE the classifier. Under v0, observation_schema() admits only .v0 payloads, so classify_denial_marker never sees an unrecognised schema on this path: returning Some(V1) for a non-triple still fails == Some(V0) and is still not a marker. This mutant cannot move any of the 14 outcomes even in theory. To measure that promise, mutate the Stage 2 match instead.

denial_marker_binding.label: 1 the origin must be the proxy
2 v1 pairs with the v1 error code
denial_marker_binding.reason: WRONG PROFILE, not a hole. The v1 schema / -31999 pairing is Stage 3 of v1.md. v0's rule for a v1 schema is the opposite of pairing: unrecognised, therefore invalid. Under v0 selection a .v1 payload never enters observations, so the V1 arm of the match is unreachable here. Its survival does not mean a stranger can ignore the v1 pairing and reproduce the v0 digest; it means the v0 corpus never presents that pairing. The v1 corpus already covers it (ok-003-cross-pair-inert).

denial_marker_binding.label: CONTROL harness reachability on the verifier path

sha256:cb58ce91863f52e0568742b977f064215.label: 1 the origin must be the proxy
sha256:cb58ce91863f52e0568742b977f064215.reason: v0 Stage 3 promises an observation is a marker only if ALL THREE legs hold: schema, code AND origin == assay-proxy, and it spells out the consequence -- an observation that is well-formed but fails the triple is valid and inert. No vector among the 14 is a well-formed v0 observation whose only defect is a wrong origin, so deleting the third leg cannot move a pinned outcome. THE GAP IS IN THE CORPUS, NOT IN THE IMPLEMENTATION. Our own tree does exercise this leg, in crates/assay-evidence/tests/denial_marker_classifier.rs::wrong_origin_is_inert, for v0 and v1 both. What the corpus cannot do is TRANSMIT the requirement: a stranger reimplementing from the published vectors plus v0.md gets no vector that fails if they skip the origin leg, and still reproduces the pinned digest. Recorded rather than fixed because adding a vector moves a digest that is a published contract carried by assay#1840.
